tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-27 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Neutral at industry level because it is split, carried. Banks: the UK Financial Policy Committee ruling is favourable for cost of equity and Jefferies (D. Farr, 26-Nov) sees 'the mother of all comebacks' into 2027, against consensus cuts and HSBC, ING and Societe Generale selling AI loans (MacroStrategy, 26-Nov); insurance was not spoken to. Relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior). Banks C and Insurance B carry the view; Alternative finance D. No change.

sector.why: Overweight, carried: higher reinvestment yields and large, simple, cash-yielding cases; insurance was not spoken to this week; relative strength B (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; C prior), agrees. Not A, because credit widening is this row's counter-case and this week it widened (AI-linked; SoftBank five-year CDS 516 basis points, Outset Global, 26-Nov) without a default wave, so the tripwire has not fired. Pool names Beazley, Hiscox, Ageas, ASR Nederland, Talanx, Vienna Insurance. To A if credit stabilises with a Nordic premium read repeated; to C on the first reported default wave.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Poland; Goldman's emerging markets team (24-Nov) is constructive on emerging markets as a group with rates near a peak, which is general, not Polish. Fourteen Pool stocks are Polish, eight of them banks, so this is still the country row most likely to move. Relative strength is not graded by country.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
